Kana

Romaji lock is on. Readings are hidden once a character is mastered. After kana is automatic, romaji slows you down.
Start here if you have never read Japanese.

Work through the lessons in order. Each one introduces five characters with a memory hook, then drills only those five until you get each of them right twice in a row. Nothing is tested before it has been taught. Two weeks of this and you can stop using romaji for good.

Vocabulary

All 1,926 words from the Japanese Core 2000 deck, imported from your own Japanese_Core_2k.apkg. Ordered by the deck's ten frequency steps, so step one is the two hundred most useful words. Every word carries native audio and a linked example sentence. Open any word to see how you do with it: meaning, reading, listening, saying it and spotting it in its sentence.

Where the words in this app come from
  • Imported, your own deck: Core 2000 (Review, Vocabulary), the iKnow Core 2000 deck from your own Anki file. Not written by this app, and not for sharing.
  • Written for this app, by an AI assistant: phrases, situations, simulations, school and home days, readings, grammar examples and replies. They were drafted by Claude (an AI) while the app was built. The situations that list Japanese sources were checked against them; everything else awaits a native speaker. Treat all of it as good but unreviewed until a teacher has looked (Settings → Content review).
  • Made while you study: nothing. The app does not generate Japanese on the fly; every line you practise is one of the above.
  • My words: words you added yourself in the Notebook.
  • Pitch accent and word types: UniDic, from Japan’s National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics.

Subtitle study

Load a video file and a subtitle track. Words in your deck become clickable.

How this works. Pick any video file on your machine and a matching subtitle file in SRT, VTT, or ASS format. Subtitles render over the video, and every word that exists in your Core 2000 deck becomes clickable for a definition, audio, and one-click queueing.

Lookup covers deck vocabulary only, not a full dictionary, so unknown words stay plain text. Streaming services that use DRM cannot be read by any browser page, so this works on local files.

Shadow mode. With subtitles loaded, the video can stop after every line: replay it, slow it down, record yourself and compare, then go on. The recording stays in this tab.

Credits

Core 2000 deck (words, sentences and native audio): iKnow, from your own Anki copy, for personal study only.

Everything else in Japanese (phrases, simulations, readings, the grammar course): written for this app by Claude, an AI assistant, and not yet reviewed by a native speaker unless a situation lists its sources.

Pitch accent: UniDic 2.1.2, copyright 2011-2013 The UniDic Consortium, used under the BSD License. About nine in ten Core words have an entry; the rest, mostly compounds, show none rather than a guess.
